phases.name: Causal Evidence
phases.outcome: Establish whether a fixed causal path can earn one fresh neural and transfer claim without reusing consumed evidence.

phases.name: Translation And Generalization
phases.outcome: Separate portability, interaction, neural contribution, and calibration rather than bundling them into one demo.

phases.name: Reliability And Confounds
phases.outcome: Measure sample efficiency, uncertainty, peripheral shortcuts, and geometry failure modes.

phases.name: Reproducibility And Local Deployment
phases.outcome: Make artifacts portable, privacy-aware, cross-machine reproducible, and eligible for a bounded edge-runtime decision.

phases.name: Live Translation And Release
phases.outcome: Join authorized replay mechanics to the token interface, qualify one device only if earned, reproduce independently, and promote only supported claims.

loops.core_question: Can every transform before the causal encoder run incrementally without future samples, evaluation-fit statistics, timestamp drift, or chunk-boundary changes?
loops.why_high_value: A causal model is not causal if filtering, resampling, padding, or normalization leaks future context; this gate protects every later streaming claim.
loops.build_deliverable: Versioned stateful preprocessing contract with a dedicated causal anti-alias SOS stage, phase-locked decimator, replay harness, transform provenance, and fail-closed refusals.
loops.research_deliverable: Pinned Brain2Qwerty-to-NeuralSet-to-MNE source trace plus filter delay, full folding-band, alias-map, resampling jitter, padding, and train-only normalization analysis.
loops.data_scope: Target-free synthetic signals first; any later S21 use is restricted to separately authorized source-train rows and may not open source-test or session-2 evidence.
controls: Seven frozen chunk schedules including whole-item, single-sample, decimation-boundary, frame-boundary, powers-of-two, and seeded-irregular splits.
Six target-free signal families, ten resume cuts, and three future-mutation cuts across physically separate seeds 2501 and 2502.
A 65,537-point 0-500 Hz response grid, 23 exact alias source probes, and complete 50-500 Hz folding-band attenuation before any fixture array opens.
Offline noncausal reference reported separately and never substituted for the causal path.
primary_metrics: right-context samples and milliseconds
valid-sample and timestamp identity
maximum offline-stream payload error
schedule hash agreement
dedicated and complete-chain folding-band attenuation plus alias destination correctness

loops.acceptance_boundary: A brain-specific claim requires brain-only performance above all preregistered non-brain controls and a positive incremental contribution over the strongest peripheral condition.
loops.stop_rule: If peripheral or timing controls explain the result, relabel it as task/peripheral decoding and block a neural claim.
loops.authorization_boundary: Planning only. No peripheral recording, device access, real signal read, or model run is authorized.
loops.resource_cap: Zero collection now; future packet must set exact files, bytes, retention, one-thread analysis, and 32 MiB derived-artifact cap.

loops.title: Geometry And Reference Harmonization
loops.core_question: Can channel geometry, names, units, reference, and missing sensors be normalized across sessions and devices without erasing provenance?
loops.why_high_value: Cross-session and cross-device failures can come from coordinate or reference mismatch rather than model capacity.
loops.build_deliverable: Versioned channel ontology, geometry transform ledger, reference/unit converter, missing-channel mask, and roundtrip validation.
loops.research_deliverable: Modality-specific coordinate-frame and referencing requirements with explicit non-equivalence rules.
loops.data_scope: Synthetic geometry fixtures and metadata sidecars first; real headers only after separate authorization and without opening signal arrays.
controls: Permutation, missing-channel, mirrored-coordinate, wrong-unit, and wrong-reference fixtures.
Original and harmonized metadata retained side by side.
No accuracy-based channel mapping on evaluation data.
primary_metrics: matched, missing, duplicate, and ambiguous channel counts
coordinate transform residual
unit and reference conversion identity
geometry availability fraction
roundtrip and provenance hashes
loops.acceptance_boundary: Proceed only when transforms are deterministic, reversible where promised, hash-bound, and refuse ambiguous geometry or reference instead of guessing.
loops.stop_rule: Keep geometry unavailable if source coordinates or frames cannot be proven; do not infer device equivalence from channel names alone.
loops.authorization_boundary: Planning only. Synthetic fixture work or real-header inspection requires a separately scoped Loop 36 authorization.
loops.resource_cap: Dependency-free core, optional MNE only inside adapters, one thread, 16 MiB artifacts, and zero signal-array reads for metadata mode.

loops.title: BIDS Derivative And Provenance Export
loops.core_question: Can caches, tokens, reports, and split metadata be exported as inspectable derivatives without copying raw data or losing source identity?
loops.why_high_value: A standards-aware derivative makes external reproduction easier while preserving the local-first raw-data boundary.
loops.build_deliverable: BIDS-derivative export plan, dataset description, GeneratedBy and SourceDatasets provenance, sidecars, path validator, and no-raw-copy audit.
loops.research_deliverable: BIDS derivative and electrophysiology mapping note identifying standard fields, extension fields, and unsupported claims.
loops.data_scope: Tiny synthetic caches and reports only for the interface proof; no real raw file is copied, packaged, or redistributed.
controls: Source, configuration, split, payload, and code hashes retained.
Path traversal, subject collision, overwrite, and raw-copy refusals.
Roundtrip validation from derivative metadata back to source artifact identity.
primary_metrics: required and unavailable field counts
source-to-derivative hash coverage
roundtrip identity
input, output, and duplicated bytes
raw-data copy count
loops.acceptance_boundary: Pass as a synthetic derivative interface only when provenance is complete, extension fields are namespaced, no raw payload is copied, and all generated files remain under cap.
loops.stop_rule: Do not claim BIDS compliance for unsupported fields or invent source metadata; export an explicit warning or refuse.
loops.authorization_boundary: Planning only. Export implementation and generated fixtures require a separate Loop 37 authorization.
loops.resource_cap: One thread, one worker, dependency-free metadata core, 16 MiB generated derivative tree, and zero real-data bytes.

loops.title: Neural Data Privacy And Lifecycle
loops.core_question: Can the project prove where sensitive recordings and embeddings live, who can access them, and how they are retained or deleted?
loops.why_high_value: Neural signals and embeddings can carry identity information; local-first behavior needs verifiable lifecycle controls, not just a promise.
loops.build_deliverable: Data inventory, sensitivity labels, local path policy, retention and deletion receipts, redaction scanner, and privacy threat model.
loops.research_deliverable: NIST-aligned privacy risk map plus EEG identity-risk review and contributor guidance.
loops.data_scope: Repository metadata and synthetic fixtures only; no identity attack, real embedding export, or participant re-identification experiment.
controls: Tracked-history and staged-secret scans.
Raw, derived, report, log, temporary, and backup lifecycle paths tested separately.
Absolute paths, participant aliases, timestamps, and device serials redacted by default.
Deletion receipt verifies expected paths without destructive broad cleanup.
primary_metrics: sensitive path and field coverage
redaction recall on generated fixtures
retention-policy violations
tracked neural payload bytes
verified deletion and unresolved copy counts
loops.acceptance_boundary: Pass when every artifact class has an owner, location, retention rule, redaction behavior, and verifiable local deletion path, with zero tracked neural payloads.
loops.stop_rule: Block data-sharing or release claims when lifecycle ownership, consent, license, or deletion cannot be proven.
loops.authorization_boundary: Planning only. No real identity analysis or destructive cleanup is authorized.
loops.resource_cap: Standard-library scanners where possible, one thread, one worker, 8 MiB reports, no real signal reads, and no network upload.

loops.title: Cross-Machine Reproducibility Matrix
loops.core_question: Which outputs are bitwise stable across supported Python and operating-system combinations, and which require explicit numerical tolerances?
loops.why_high_value: Open-source users need to know whether a mismatch is a bug, a backend difference, or an unsupported environment.
loops.build_deliverable: CI matrix, environment manifest, golden semantic hashes, tolerance registry, failure diagnostics, and artifact reproducibility report.
loops.research_deliverable: Reproducibility policy distinguishing semantic identity, numerical compatibility, timing comparison, and environment-specific evidence.
loops.data_scope: Dependency-free tests and authorized synthetic fixtures only; no real or consumed cache, target, or model training access.
controls: At least macOS and Linux where CI capacity permits.
Base and optional-neuro environments kept separate.
Bitwise semantic fields tested separately from floating payload tolerances.
Tolerance changes require a recorded failing environment and explicit decision.
primary_metrics: matrix pass rate
semantic hash agreement
maximum numerical drift
runtime and peak RSS by environment
artifact and dependency size
loops.acceptance_boundary: Pass when every supported cell either reproduces the registered contract or fails with an explicit unsupported reason; no tolerance is widened after hidden evaluation access.
loops.stop_rule: Do not claim cross-machine reproducibility from one host; quarantine platform-specific drift until diagnosed and documented.
loops.authorization_boundary: Planning only. New matrix jobs, fixtures, and optional installs require a separate bounded Loop 39 change.
loops.resource_cap: One thread per job, no large cache, 32 MiB job artifacts, and existing CI time limits.

loops.title: Edge Runtime Packaging Gate
loops.core_question: Can one already qualified frozen pipeline be packaged for an edge runtime while preserving outputs, state, timestamps, and measured resource behavior?
loops.why_high_value: Packaging is meaningful only after correctness and local runtime gates; it can then reveal startup, delegate, memory-planning, and operator support constraints.
loops.build_deliverable: Single-backend export contract, operator audit, packaged artifact validator, reference comparison, and startup/runtime/RSS report.
loops.research_deliverable: ExecuTorch or alternative edge-runtime decision note based on supported operators and target platform, not trend appeal.
loops.data_scope: Frozen target-free synthetic fixture only; no real data, consumed targets, retraining, or architecture changes.
controls: Reference eager path retained.
Exact frame, timestamp, decoder trace, and state comparison.
Fallback and undelegated operator counts reported.
Package size, load time, steady-state time, and peak memory separated.
primary_metrics: behavioral identity and numerical drift
package and tensor bytes
startup, producer, decoder, and full-pipeline latency
peak RSS and planned memory
delegated, fallback, and unsupported operator counts
loops.acceptance_boundary: Adopt a package only if a previously qualified reference behavior is preserved, unsupported fallback is zero or explicitly accepted, and a preregistered deployment benefit passes.
loops.stop_rule: Park packaging if it requires retraining, architecture changes, hidden fallback, or more resources without a measured benefit; do not call desktop packaging portable hardware.
loops.authorization_boundary: Planning only. No export, conversion, optional edge dependency, inference, profiler, or package generation is authorized.
loops.resource_cap: One backend, one thread, one worker, 32 MiB generated package and reports, 60 seconds per measurement worker, and 1 GiB peak RSS.

loops.title: RW3 Stream-To-NeuroToken Integration
loops.core_question: Can an authorized source-chunk replay pass through causal preprocessing into NeuroTokenCache without timestamp, gap, state, or schedule drift?
loops.why_high_value: This joins the acquisition contract to the model interface while keeping replay mechanics separate from hardware and decoding claims.
loops.build_deliverable: Source-chunk to preprocessing to NeuroToken adapter, resume state, gap propagation, schedule matrix, and end-to-end provenance hashes.
loops.research_deliverable: Clock-domain and latency ledger mapping source, corrected, arrival, preprocessing, token, decoder, and render times.
loops.data_scope: Only future authorized target-free RW3 synthetic replay; no BrainFlow, LSL, PyXDF, socket, live source, hardware, or real recording unless separately staged later.
controls: Canonical offline path and every authorized chunk schedule.
Gap, duplicate, reorder, reconnect, and reset fixtures.
Raw, corrected, and arrival clocks kept distinct.
Resume from serialized state compared with uninterrupted replay.
primary_metrics: source, preprocessing, and token semantic hash agreement
timestamp and valid-length identity
gap and anomaly propagation
state bytes and resume identity
stage runtime, scheduling delay, peak RSS, and output bytes
loops.acceptance_boundary: Pass only when every authorized schedule and resume path preserves canonical tokens and provenance, and anomalies remain explicit rather than repaired silently.
loops.stop_rule: Any timestamp collapse, silent interpolation, lost anomaly, schedule-dependent token, or state mismatch parks integration before live or device work.
loops.authorization_boundary: Planning only. This roadmap does not authorize RW3 Stage A or any adapter, fixture, source-chunk, stream, or token runtime.
loops.resource_cap: One thread and worker, 32 MiB generated target-free artifacts, 60 seconds per worker, and 1 GiB peak RSS.

loops.title: One-Device Qualification
loops.core_question: Can one named device preserve declared channels, units, clocks, packets, and privacy from recorded replay through a bounded local session?
loops.why_high_value: One measured device is more credible than broad compatibility claims based on SDK imports or vendor tables.
loops.build_deliverable: Device descriptor, consent and locality checklist, recorded-versus-live equivalence packet, loss/reconnect stress report, and compatibility-level decision.
loops.research_deliverable: Device-specific timestamp, unit, reference, geometry, firmware, and data-retention review.
loops.data_scope: One separately approved board or headset, one local synthetic or consented non-sensitive qualification session, and no decoding target unless separately approved.
controls: SDK synthetic or playback source before physical hardware.
Recorded and live paths compared under the same source-chunk contract.
Packet loss, reconnect, clock reset, and buffer-drain stress cases.
Network-off and local-storage audit.
primary_metrics: channel, unit, rate, and packet identity
clock offset, jitter, gaps, duplicates, and reorder counts
capture-to-arrival timing boundary
runtime, peak RSS, bytes, and dropped samples
privacy and retention violations
loops.acceptance_boundary: Qualify only the named device, firmware, transport, host, and tested compatibility level; connectivity alone cannot qualify signal quality or decoding.
loops.stop_rule: Park physical qualification on ambiguous consent, cloud dependence, hidden timestamps, unstable identity, unsafe retention, or failed replay equivalence.
loops.authorization_boundary: Planning only. No SDK import, device discovery, socket, stream, board, hardware, or recording session is authorized.
loops.resource_cap: One device, one host, one thread for analysis, exact session and byte cap in a future packet, 32 MiB derived artifacts, and no cloud upload.

loops.title: Independent Reproduction Challenge
loops.core_question: Can an independent contributor reproduce a bounded claim from documented inputs without private guidance or sharing neural recordings?
loops.why_high_value: Independent reproduction tests the developer experience, evidence contracts, and contribution path more honestly than another maintainer-run demo.
loops.build_deliverable: Challenge packet, fixture manifest, expected semantic checks, environment capture, blinded result card, and discrepancy triage workflow.
loops.research_deliverable: Reproduction protocol distinguishing exact replication, computational reproduction, and extension on contributor-owned data.
loops.data_scope: Public code plus tiny synthetic fixtures by default; contributors keep any owned EEG local and submit metadata/aggregate reports only.
controls: Maintainer and contributor environments recorded independently.
Expected results hidden where needed until submission hash freezes.
No private recording, secret, absolute path, or participant identifier in the submission.
Negative and failed reproductions retained.
primary_metrics: semantic and numerical reproduction rate
setup time and command count
environment and warning completeness
discrepancy classes
contributor artifact bytes and privacy findings
loops.acceptance_boundary: Pass when at least one independent environment reproduces the registered artifact contract and a discrepancy, if any, is resolved or documented without moving the claim boundary.
loops.stop_rule: Do not promote a result that depends on undocumented maintainer state, private hand edits, leaked data, or an unreviewed tolerance change.
loops.authorization_boundary: Planning only. No outreach, external data exchange, or challenge execution is authorized by the roadmap file.
loops.resource_cap: Tiny public fixtures only, one-thread reference commands, 32 MiB submission cap, and no neural recording upload.

loops.title: Claim Promotion And Release Decision
loops.core_question: Which engineering and scientific claims have earned promotion into a release, and which remain fixture-backed, negative, unavailable, parked, or killed?
loops.why_high_value: The roadmap should end in an evidence decision, not an accumulation of features or optimistic wording.
loops.build_deliverable: Machine-readable evidence matrix, model and dataset cards, release checklist, claim diff, risk register, and signed proceed, park, or kill decision.
loops.research_deliverable: Release and reporting policy grounded in model cards, datasheets, privacy, licensing, and reproducibility evidence.
loops.data_scope: Artifact-only synthesis of closed loop reports; no raw, consumed, target, model, training, device, or network operation.
controls: Every claim links to a cohort, split, comparator, uncertainty, resource, and access record.
Negative results and unavailable fields remain visible.
Engineering capability and scientific performance are stated separately.
Clinical, arbitrary-thought, portable-hardware, and real-time claims default to unavailable.
primary_metrics: claims promoted, parked, killed, and unavailable
evidence-card completeness
unresolved privacy, license, security, and reproducibility blockers
artifact and documentation link integrity
release test and CI status
loops.acceptance_boundary: Release only the subset whose exact evidence cards, licenses, privacy controls, independent reproduction, tests, and claim language pass; all other claims stay explicitly unestablished.
loops.stop_rule: Hold the release rather than soften a failed gate, omit a negative comparator, or convert an engineering interface proof into a decoding claim.
loops.authorization_boundary: Planning only. The future release decision cannot retroactively authorize or upgrade any earlier experiment.
loops.resource_cap: Artifact-only review, one thread, one worker, 16 MiB generated reports, zero data/model/training/device access, and complete link/test checks.
